clue.text: National course? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter of the course is dropped

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A question about a country's own racing venue, minus its opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' strips the A from ASCOT, a British racecourse near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Bird drops core when on the rise

indicators.note: drops core says the central letter of the bird's name is removed

parts.note: the waxwing is a crested songbird

explanation.surface: A bird sheds something as it climbs into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops core' removes the middle W of the seven-letter WAXWING.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is said to be waxing as it grows, so increasing or on the up.

clue.text: Provide efficiencies — just two courses

parts.note: a stream is a course of water
a line is a course or route taken

explanation.surface: A management consultant's advice to cut the menu to just two courses.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to make a process simpler and more efficient.

clue.text: Catchphrase a big hit with Central Bank

parts.note: a slog is a hard, wild hit, as in cricket

indicators.note: central asks for the middle letters of the word bank

explanation.surface: A bank's governor coins a memorable phrase that becomes a smash.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase used in advertising or politics, a catchphrase.

clue.text: Dish has base changed for second course

indicators.note: the base of a word is its final letter, which is swapped for another

parts.note: syllabub is a creamy whipped dessert

explanation.surface: A menu note that one dish is replaced by another as the next course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has base changed for' swaps the last B of SYLLABUB for S. The definition 'course' is a course of study, not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the outline of topics for a course of study.

clue.text: Jack Ruby, say, on the slab

parts.note: a jack is a flag flown on a ship
a ruby is an example of a precious stone

explanation.surface: Jack Ruby, the man who shot Lee Harvey Oswald, lying on a mortuary slab.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a flat paving slab.

clue.text: Set course for a vintage trip

indicators.note: a trip suggests stumbling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Planning the route for an outing in a classic car.
explanation.definitionFit: To navigate is to plot and steer a course.

clue.text: Set and course constituent?

parts.note: in tennis several of these make up a set, and pheasant or venison served at dinner can make up a course

explanation.definitionFit: Games build a tennis set, and game birds or venison form a dish at a meal.

clue.text: Raw soldier enrolled in French course

indicators.note: enrolled in says one piece is placed within another

parts.note: raw weather is chilly
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant stands for soldier

explanation.surface: A green recruit signing up to train at a French institution.
explanation.walkthrough: Chantilly is a racecourse north of Paris; 'course' here is a racing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly hosts a celebrated racecourse in France.

clue.text: Climber may be obsessive about carrying one

indicators.note: carrying says one piece holds another inside it
about says the word for obsessive is turned round

parts.note: anal is slang for fussily obsessive
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mountaineer who can be obsessive about the gear they carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ANAL into LANA, and 'carrying' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests.

clue.text: Poet's rejected material

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, says the poet's name is read backwards

parts.note: T. S. Eliot was a poet

explanation.surface: A poet's discarded drafts or writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a linen or cotton fabric, often printed with scenes.

clue.text: Set fire to big banger

parts.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does
to ignite is to set alight or fire

explanation.surface: An instruction to light a huge firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a powerful explosive, so a large bang-maker.

clue.text: Army unit fails to complete the course

indicators.note: fails to complete says the last letter is missing

parts.note: a regiment is a unit of an army

explanation.surface: A military unit drops out before finishing its training course.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment.

clue.text: Artist set up by judges

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word set is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A painter framed by a panel of judges.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or evaluate it, so rates is a verb for judges.

clue.text: Sustained fire from soldiers aboard boat

indicators.note: aboard says the soldiers are inside the vessel

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Troops on a boat keep up a steady volley.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy continuous bombardment of artillery.

clue.text: View inside set (diagram attached)

parts.note: a radio is a set, a receiver
a graph is a diagram plotting data

explanation.surface: A diagram attached to a television set to show how it works inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph is an X-ray image that shows the inside of the body.

clue.text: Bird about to pass over

indicators.note: over says the pieces are turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to pass, or pass away, is to die

explanation.surface: A bird about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RE + DIE back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: They may be broken on pitch with odd soil

parts.note: pitch is the black tar used on roads

indicators.note: odd asks for the odd-placed letters of soil

explanation.surface: Things that might snap when you play on a pitch with uneven ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The bones of the ankle, the tarsi, can be broken on a bad pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsi are the ankle bones, which can be fractured.

clue.text: Material for Thatcher's first organ piece

parts.note: reeds are the material a roof thatcher uses
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: Something Margaret Thatcher had first at a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher's' wants to be Margaret Thatcher; it is a roof thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed stop is an organ stop whose pipes sound with a vibrating reed.

clue.text: Discharge rider holding certificate

indicators.note: holding says one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a rider is an addition, as a PS is to a letter
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A horseman's discharge papers held with a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the UK film rating for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pus is matter discharged from an infected wound.

clue.text: Frame shy jockey consumed by resentment

indicators.note: consumed by says one piece is swallowed inside another

parts.note: pique is resentment from wounded pride

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, so the letters are shifted about

explanation.surface: A timid jockey eaten up by bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jockey' turns SHY into HYS, which goes inside PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A physique is a person's bodily build, their frame.

clue.text: Terror suspect remanded when dodgy men disappear

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, so the letters of remanded are rearranged

explanation.surface: A terrorism suspect is held in custody while shady men vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappear' takes the letters of MEN, in any order ('dodgy'), out of REMANDED; 'suspect' rearranges the leftover RADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, much like terror.

clue.text: Set a course, perhaps, with divine surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to scry is to divine the future using a crystal
ENE, east-north-east, is a compass course

explanation.surface: Plotting a route among heavenly surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a verb, foretelling, not holy. Set is a theatre set.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage set is the scenery for a play.

clue.text: Changing course on river is cathartic

indicators.note: changing says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Altering the course of a river is emotionally freeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is an old word for a purgative medicine, which a cathartic is too.

clue.text: Set out on course for wide open space

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of set are scrambled

parts.note: PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a university degree course

explanation.surface: Setting off on a hike across a vast landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland plain, as in Russia.

clue.text: Rake over tops of beds looking for money

indicators.note: over says one piece covers the other

parts.note: a rake is a roue, a dissolute man

indicators.note: tops of asks for the first letters of beds and looking

explanation.surface: A womaniser scans the beds in search of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the Russian unit of currency.

clue.text: Two sets of players embrace a discard

indicators.note: embrace says the two groups hold the letter between them

parts.note: a cast is the set of actors in a play
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: Two teams hugging and then dropping someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aside is to throw away or reject, to discard.

clue.text: Patient horse taken from course

indicators.note: taken from says a letter is removed from the course

parts.note: a chase is a steeplechase course
H is slang shorthand for horse, heroin

explanation.surface: A sick horse led away from a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a patient being treated by a doctor.

clue.text: A union overturned cuts

indicators.note: in a down clue overturned says the word is read upside down

parts.note: union is sexual union

explanation.surface: A trade union is overturned and cuts jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut, so axes means cuts.

clue.text: Adult leaves dance course

indicators.note: leaves says the letter departs from the word

parts.note: the rhumba is a Latin dance
A is the old British film rating for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up walks out of a dance class.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhumb is a ship's course on a constant compass bearing.

clue.text: A little climber manages narrow path

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountaineer gets along a narrow ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A berm is a narrow ledge or path beside a canal or embankment.

clue.text: See 6
Disliked hanging uniform in a foreign tree

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in says the letter is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An unpopular uniformed man hanged in a tree abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging' just links: U goes inside UN + POPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpopular means disliked by most people.
